//: LibreLane configuration. Base: the Tiny Tapeout CMOS5L template (Apache-2.0). Changes from the template are marked with a //<name> comment key next to them. See NOTICE.md for the origin of the memory-block settings.
//meta: Adds one step after the power-grid generator: it runs the tile's Metal4 power stripes across the memory blocks so they are powered. The step is in librelane_plugin_jsasic_pdn.py and odb_stripes.py at the repository root.
//synth: Synthesis recipe. The first four-engine run used DELAY 4 (not set here, so the flow's own default) and got 0.497 mm2 of cells including 9,559 buffers; AREA 0 gives 0.41 mm2 with almost none, and the tile has too little routing room for the larger netlist (three routing layers, of which only Metal3 runs left to right).
//routability: Off. When on, global placement inflates cells wherever it predicts routing congestion; on this tile it predicted congestion nearly everywhere, inflated the cells by 76% and left no legal position for the last ones (the first four-engine run stopped with 'Detailed placement failed'). Spreading the cells also lengthens the wires, which is the opposite of what the shortage of Metal3 needs.
//drt: Stop detailed routing after 12 passes instead of 64. In a local trial of one engine the violation count was down to 2 by pass 8; one that is not would otherwise run into the 6-hour job limit.
//clock: 16.66 ns = 60 MHz, the project's target clock.
//pdn: Power stripes matched to the memory block's supply columns (11.24 um pitch, VDD and VSS 5.62 um apart). Width 2.1 + spacing 3.52 = 5.62; pitch 44.96 = 4 x 11.24; offset 6.15 puts the first VPWR stripe centre at x = 9.03, which is the first supply column of a block placed at x = 3.36 (or 3.36 plus a whole number of pitches). Template values were pitch 50.0, width 2.1.
//pdn_cfg: LibreLane's power-grid script without its per-block grid, which has no shapes on a single-layer grid and makes the generator fail. The blocks get their power from Project.ExtendPowerStripes instead.
//stripes: Every-other mode: the tile grid's stripe pairs plus a pair on every other column pair of each bit-cell array.
//halo: Keeps standard cells away from the memory blocks' edges.
//drc: Magic reads the memory blocks from their abstract and reports the power stripes crossing them as overlaps. DRC is done by KLayout with the CMOS5L deck instead, which sees the real layout.
//macros: Four IHP single-port memory blocks, one per engine: three of 256 x 32 (416.64 x 118.78 um) and, for engine 2, one of 512 x 32 (416.64 x 191.34 um; same width and the same power columns). Two sit on the bottom edge (orientation FS, pin edge on top) and two on the top edge (orientation N, pin edge at the bottom), so every pin edge faces the logic. The top-left block starts at x = 273.12 to leave the tile's own pins (top edge, x = 30 to 191) clear. Every x is 3.36 + 134.88 * k: 134.88 um is 3 power-stripe pitches (44.96) and 281 routing tracks (0.48), so each block sits on the stripes and on the routing grid exactly as the block at x = 3.36 did in the probe build. Every y is a multiple of the 3.78 um row height. Corner names are LibreLane's; the blocks' fast corner was characterized at -55 C.
//pdn_connect: Tells the power-grid tools that each block's VDD!, VDDARRAY! and VSS! pins are the tile's VPWR and VGND.
//obstructions: No signal routing across the memory blocks on any routing layer (the tile routes on Metal2 to Metal4 only). One rectangle per block and layer, equal to the block's footprint.
